title: Benchmark registry (Content-Grounding §6.3)
description: Governed 'what good looks like' references — the third comparison axis. A benchmark is either NORMATIVE (a defined standard that applies universally, e.g. world-class OEE) or EMPIRICAL (a peer distribution that only means anything against an industry — those MUST carry per-industry segments). Every entry references a real KPI, needs an authoritative source (not a headcount of blogs), and records the observed range.

kpi_id.description: Must resolve to a governed KPI under core/kpi_catalog/kpis/ (Golden Thread).

benchmark_class.description: normative = a defined standard (world-class OEE), universally applicable. empirical = a peer distribution (NPS, conversion) that requires per-industry `segments` to be decision-useful.

value.description: Normative: the standard. Empirical: the cross-industry central tendency — a labelled FALLBACK, use the matching segment when the industry is known.

segments.description: Per-industry values — required for empirical benchmarks (a cross-industry average misleads a specific client).

sources.description: ≥2 sources, ≥1 of which is authoritative (tier primary or large_sample) — not a headcount of secondary blogs restating each other.

tier.description: primary = originator/definitional; large_sample = big-N study; secondary = aggregator/commentary.
